title: The cue changes the stage
summary: Let the producer operate the lighting designer's portfolio through the selected cue. The stage itself is the work sample.

layout.skeleton: Lead with a short identity and one cinematic proscenium. Set a named cue inspector beside the stage on wide screens and directly below it on mobile.
layout.focus: An original performer mid-gesture and its long shadow make the direction of each light visible. Show light spilling across the backcloth and slanting across the floor.
layout.desktop: Start the stage within 144 CSS px of the top at 1440 × 900. Compose the full stage, the three cue controls and current technique within the initial viewport.
layout.mobile: Give the figure at least 45% of the stage height at 390 px and keep the tip of the shadow inside the frame. Keep the visible Choose a cue label, three controls and technique close below.
layout.rhythm: Make the header a compact masthead, with a 48–64 px identity on desktop and a single title line or two short lines on mobile. Give the remaining height to the stage.

imagery.subject: Draw an expressive human performer reaching into the light. Shape the arm, bent leg and flowing fabric as one recognizable silhouette. Keep that pose fixed and let shadows and lit fabric distinguish the three cues.
imagery.crop: Compose a genuine 390 px view with a larger performer and legible, sharply drawn floor shadow. Preserve the beam and shadow tips on mobile.
imagery.fallback: Use three original stills composed with the same stage framing and pose. Describe each light effect in accessible text.

motion.effect: Switch the scene, technique text and filled selection immediately. Fade in only the selected cue marker.
motion.reduced: Switch the light, current cue text, and underline immediately.

action.instruction: Label the group Choose a cue. Use native buttons with aria-pressed. Give the selected cue a persistent plum fill, light text and a lamp marker even when unfocused. Give focus its own two-tone outline. Update the image description and printed technique together.
action.label: Use the actual cue name

why: The first interaction demonstrates the actual craft and lets a producer compare techniques without finding a separate demo.

sources.observation: Driving the car demonstrates the creative developer's work while the visitor explores the portfolio. The site lists a map, respawn and multiple input methods.
The studio offers standard Work and Connect navigation alongside an optional themed command interface.

credit: Original stage composition inspired by Bruno Simon and ToyFight. Use only original artwork.

title: The river changes the town
summary: Build the story along one measurable cross-section. A selectable elevation changes the illustrated bank and the list of affected places.

layout.skeleton: Build one flood chart with exactly three contour lines, ordered by elevation. Align a readable place label and original marker to each threshold. Put the level controls and current closure list beside the chart.
layout.focus: Show a real river section with a low path on the bank, a ferry beside its middle landing, and a footbridge spanning the water at the upper mark. A single waterline changes which labeled places close.
layout.desktop: Give the selected elevation and all current closures room in the reading column. Keep the contour chart and result within the initial 1440 × 900 view.
layout.mobile: Place the explicit level selector and complete current closure list before the chart so the entire task result is visible inside the initial 390 × 844 view. Follow with a 240–300 px cross-section and three 16 px place labels.
layout.rhythm: Give the answer and the three level controls the first reading position on mobile. Use the equal elevation steps to space the contours below.

imagery.subject: Draw the path as a cut in the low bank, the boat beside its mid-level landing, and the bridge crossing the channel. Point each clear place label at its drawing. Use blue #A4CBE7 for unreached space and ochre #EFBE61 for closed places alongside text.
imagery.crop: Keep all three structures and thresholds distinct at 390 px. Use legible 16 px place labels. Keep the complete current closure result and controls above the compact chart on mobile.
imagery.fallback: Keep the three contour lines, their readable place names and the live closure list. Simplify the drawing before reducing text size.

motion.effect: Snap the waterline and closure labels to the selected level together. Give only the new level marker one brief emphasis.
motion.reduced: Use the immediate new level and matching list without the marker animation.

action.instruction: Use named native controls for the exact elevations, expose the selected level and list all closures at or below it in readable text.
action.label: Use each supplied level and its units

why: The water line makes the relationship between height and closures visible. The text and controls still let a visitor answer the question quickly.

sources.observation: The ascent orders the exhibits by real altitude. The Kármán line is one of the named markers.
Depth provides the organizing scale of an explorable ocean story.

credit: Original river cross-section inspired by Neal Agarwal's single-axis stories.
